items.title: Top 5 Longest Years in the Solar System (#1 Lasts 11,400 Years) #shorts
items.description:
One year = one trip around the Sun. Five far worlds, their orbits drawn to scale.
Full video: How Long to Reach Every Planet? By Car, Neptune Takes 4,912 Years

Sources
• NASA Science (Pluto): one orbit takes 248 Earth years; Pluto was discovered in 1930
• NASA Science (Haumea): one orbit takes about 285 Earth years; its fast spin stretches it into an elongated shape
• JPL Small-Body Database: Makemake orbital period about 309 years; Eris about 557 years; Sedna about 11,400 years (semi-major axis about 506 AU, eccentricity about 0.85)
• Farming began roughly 12,000 to 11,000 years ago (Neolithic Revolution, Encyclopaedia Britannica)
• Own calculations: Kepler's third law P = a^1.5 (years, AU) as a check; 1930 + 248 = 2178; 2026 - 309 = 1717; 557 / 250 (USA since 1776) ≈ 2.2; 11,400 / 248 ≈ 46

Visuals are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
#shorts #space #solarsystem #science

items.title: The Moon's Entire Orbit Fits Inside the Sun #shorts
items.description:
Put Earth at the centre of the Sun: the Moon's whole orbit fits inside, with 311,600 km to spare. Drawn to scale.
Full video: What If the Moon Crashed Into Earth? You'd Have 4 Days

Sources
• NASA Science, Sun facts: the Sun is about 1,392,000 km (865,000 miles) wide, so its radius is about 696,000 km
• NASA Science, Moon facts: average distance from Earth 384,400 km (about 405,500 km at its farthest)
• NASA, Apollo 11 mission timeline: launch 16 July 1969, entered lunar orbit 19 July 1969 (about 76 hours)
• Own calculations: 696,000 - 384,400 = 311,600 km to spare (290,500 km with the Moon at its farthest); 1,392,000 / 768,800 ≈ 1.8; Apollo 11 average pace 384,400 km / 76 h ≈ 5,060 km/h, so 1,392,000 km takes about 275 h ≈ 11.5 days

Visuals are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
#shorts #space #sun #moon #scale

items.title: Voyager 1 Is Now 1 Light-Day Away. A Message Takes 24 Hours
items.description:
On 18 November 2026, Voyager 1 became the first human-made object one light-day from Earth: about 25.9 billion km. We send one radio message and ride along with it, hour by hour, from the Moon in 1.3 seconds to Voyager at hour 24, and see what Voyager found at every stop.

Chapters
0:00 A message that takes a full day
0:40 Stop 1: leaving Earth
0:55 1.3 seconds: the Moon, 8 minutes: the Sun
1:12 43 minutes: Jupiter and Io's volcanoes
1:48 79 minutes: Saturn, and the Titan choice
2:16 4 hours: Neptune's orbit
2:37 5.6 hours: the Pale Blue Dot
3:11 9.6 hours: the most distant object ever made
3:28 13 hours: the termination shock
3:46 16.8 hours: interstellar space
4:25 24 hours: Voyager 1
4:45 The reply is a whisper
5:19 Monday to Wednesday: fixing it from 24 light-hours
5:39 The power clock
6:18 The Oort cloud, Gliese 445 and the Golden Record
7:00 The twist: 1,549 light-days to the nearest star
7:26 Recap and next episode

Sources
• NASA/JPL: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day (about 25.9 billion km, 16.1 billion miles) from Earth on 18 November 2026, about 10:16 UTC; a command sent Monday morning gets an answer Wednesday morning (mission manager Suzy Dodd); public event: flash V-G-R in Morse code
• NASA/JPL: Voyager 1 launched 5 September 1977; Jupiter flyby March 1979 (active volcanoes discovered on Io); Saturn flyby November 1980 with a close pass by Titan that sent it out of the plane of the planets
• NASA/JPL: Pale Blue Dot, 14 February 1990, about 6 billion km; Earth is about 0.12 of a pixel; the cameras were turned off soon after
• NASA/JPL: Voyager 1 crossed the termination shock in December 2004 (about 94 AU) and the heliopause on 25 August 2012 (about 121 AU); Voyager 2 crossed it on 5 November 2018
• NASA: the solar wind blows at about 400 km/s; Voyager 1 travels at about 17 km/s
• NASA/JPL: Voyager's transmitter radiates about 22 W; data rate 160 bits per second; about 69.63 KB of memory across its computers
• NASA/JPL: flight data system memory chip failure (November 2023) worked around by relocating code; engineering and science data restored by April and June 2024
• NASA/JPL: radioisotope power about 470 W at launch, about 4 W lost per year; instruments switched off to save power, Low-Energy Charged Particles instrument off on 17 April 2026; Voyager 1 has two science instruments still operating
• NASA: about 300 years to the inner edge of the Oort Cloud and possibly 30,000 years to fly beyond it; in about 40,000 years Voyager 1 passes within about 1.6 light-years of Gliese 445
• NASA/JPL: Voyager 2 launched 20 August 1977, Voyager 1 on 5 September 1977 on a faster trajectory; Voyager 1 overtook Pioneer 10 as the most distant human-made object on 17 February 1998
• S. K. Ocker et al., Nature Astronomy (2021): a persistent, faint plasma wave signal in interstellar space detected by Voyager 1's plasma wave instrument
• NASA/JPL: the Golden Record carries greetings in 55 languages, sounds of Earth, about 90 minutes of music and images
• Proxima Centauri is about 4.24 light-years away (NASA)
• Own calculations: 1 light-day = 299,792.458 km/s × 86,400 s ≈ 25.9 billion km ≈ 173.1 AU; light time 499 s per AU (Jupiter 5.2 AU ≈ 43 min, Saturn 9.5 AU ≈ 79 min, 6 billion km ≈ 5.6 h, 94 AU ≈ 13 h, 121 AU ≈ 16.8 h); speed check (173.1 - 121) AU in 14.2 years ≈ 3.66 AU/yr ≈ 17.4 km/s; received power estimate from a free-space link budget (22 W, 8.4 GHz, 3.7 m and 70 m dishes) ≈ 4 × 10^-19 W; 128 GB / 69.63 KB ≈ 1.8 million; 4.24 ly × 365.25 ≈ 1,549 light-days; 4.24 ly at 17 km/s ≈ 75,000 years; 1 / 1,549 ≈ 0.06%; 173.1 AU / 3.6 AU per year ≈ 48 years per extra light-day

—
Cosmic Scale: the universe, measured in a way you can feel.

Visuals and animations are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.

items.title: A Message to Voyager 1 Takes 24 Hours. The Nearest Star Is 1,549 Times Farther #shorts
items.description:
Voyager 1 is now one light-day from Earth. After 49 years of flight, the nearest star is still about 1,549 light-days away.
Full video: Voyager 1 Is Now 1 Light-Day Away. A Message Takes 24 Hours

Sources
• NASA/JPL: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day (about 25.9 billion km) from Earth on 18 November 2026; speed about 17 km/s
• NASA: Proxima Centauri is about 4.24 light-years away
• Own calculations: 4.24 × 365.25 ≈ 1,549 light-days; 4.24 light-years at 17 km/s ≈ 75,000 years

Visuals are original. Narration uses a synthetic voice.
#shorts #space #voyager1 #nasa
